page: Amazon Web Services t9g.medium is a burstable general purpose virtual machine powered by AWS Graviton processors on the arm64 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz, with a single thread per core. Memory capacity is fixed at 4.0 GB total, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware accelerators are not present, with zero discrete GPUs included. The t9g.medium configuration contains no local storage volumes, requiring network-attached storage for persistent operational data. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 0 Gbps, meaning the instance relies on dynamic network bursting rather than high continuous throughput, and it includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The arm64 Graviton foundation delivers qualitative energy and cost efficiency compared to legacy architectures for low-duty tasks. Because this instance uses a burstable CPU model with no attached local disk, it entails tradeoffs in sustained peak throughput. The configuration fits light microservices, test and staging environments, low-traffic web servers, utility automation, and intermittent batch jobs.
